subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should command-lane aging preserve fresh foreground/user priority when aged normal/default work has waited past the threshold?
rationale: The choice defines the scheduler fairness contract for existing sessions: capping normal aging preserves foreground latency, while allowing normal to age into foreground gives stronger anti-starvation but changes user-facing ordering.

options.title: Repair foreground-preserving aging
options.body: Cap or explicitly rank aged work so fresh foreground/user tasks still win, then add aged-normal versus foreground coverage and real proof.

options.title: Accept stronger aging
options.body: Allow aged lower/default work to overtake foreground, but update code comments, tests, PR text, and linked issue triage to state that latency tradeoff.

options.title: Defer to scheduler design
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want aging, foreground reservation, and broader gateway fairness decided together.

recommendation.title: Repair foreground-preserving aging
recommendation.body: Cap or explicitly rank aged work so fresh foreground/user tasks still win, then add aged-normal versus foreground coverage and real proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The queue history and overlapping scheduler-policy PR make this the best available owner for the product-direction choice.
